subject: DPA: clarifications on subprocessors and EU->US transfer mechanism
messages:
From: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@finservco.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@finservco.com
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Data Processing Addendum - questions on subprocessors & transfers

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to follow up on the DPA template attached (Customer_DPA_Template.pdf). Our privacy counsel has two quick asks before we can circulate for signature:

1) Subprocessors: we need a commitment on notification timing when Redwood engages new subprocessors that will process EEA personal data (customer-facing restriction clause). Is 60 days acceptable?
2) Transfers: the template references EU Standard Contractual Clauses but also allows other mechanisms. For our legal team it would be helpful to confirm whether Redwood intends to rely on SCCs (2021) or an alternative (e.g., adequacy + internal addendum). If SCCs, please confirm Redwood will complete the controller-processor Annex and provide a copy.

Can you share a redline and your current subprocessor list? Also, do you support e-signature (DocuSign) for execution?

Best,
Marta
Marta Lopez
Privacy Counsel, FinServCo

Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 10:04:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Data Processing Addendum - questions on subprocessors & transfers

Hi Marta — thanks for the clear asks and the template.

Quick answers up front:
- Subprocessor notification: we typically send notice 30 days prior to onboarding a new subprocessor that will process EEA data, and we can accept a 30-day notification clause in the DPA. We understand some customers request longer windows; if 60 days is a hard requirement for FinServCo, we can discuss, but that will require an escalation.
- Transfers: Redwood intends to rely on the EU SCCs (2021) for controller-processor transfers; we will complete the relevant Annex and share it as part of the DPA package.

I've attached our initial redline (RW_DPA_Redline_v1.docx) with the edits Marcus and I suggest — mainly:
- Replace the current transfer paragraph with explicit SCC Annex reference
- Add an annexed subprocessor list and a 30-day notification clause with right to object
- Minor language on data retention and audit access

Marcus and Neha — could you review the redline and legal comments before I send this back to Marta?

Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

-- attachment: RW_DPA_Redline_v1.docx (Word, 86 KB)

Subject: Re: Data Processing Addendum - questions on subprocessors & transfers

Laura — quick legal notes inline. For Marta's team: I'm copying the version with tracked comments (legal_comments_marcus_v1.pdf). High level:

- SCCs: we accept SCCs (2021). We'll complete the Processor Annex. We prefer to keep the DPA as the controlling document and include the completed Annex as an exhibit.
- Notification window: 30 days is Redwood standard; 60 days is unusually long for cloud-native services and can materially impact our ability to onboard optimizations in time. If FinServCo requires 60 days, we will need to limit scope (e.g., exclude certain ephemeral subprocessors) or accept a compromise (45 days).
- Subprocessor list: we can provide a current list and a defined cadence for updates (quarterly published list + immediate notice of security-critical changes).
- Audit: we will provide SOC2 reports and conduct remote assessments; on-site audits are limited to specific enterprise contracts.

If procurement pushes on the 60-day ask, propose: 45 days + emergency exception for security fixes with immediate notice. That usually moves things forward.

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Hi Laura / Marcus,

Thanks — that is helpful. A few follow-ups from our privacy counsel attached (FinServCo_Security_Questionnaire.pdf):

- FinServCo prefers a 60-day notice for any subprocessor that will process regulated customer data; however, we are open to 45 days if Redwood provides an escalation path and guarantees immediate notice for security-related subprocessors.
- Regarding SCCs: counsel asks that Redwood provide the completed controller-processor Annex (including roles, export mechanisms and technical measures). Please upload the completed Annex or include it in the next redline.
- Execution: procurement prefers DocuSign. Can Redwood send a DocuSign link when the final DPA is ready?

Also attaching our security questionnaire for your ops/security team to confirm controls.

Best,
Marta

- Subprocessor notification: 45-day notice for general onboarding; immediate notice for security-critical subprocessors and a short objection window.
- Annex: completed controller-processor Annex included as Exhibit A (technical & organizational measures described).
- Audit & reports: SOC 2 Type II to be provided; remote assessments accepted.
- Execution: we will route the attached DPA via DocuSign. Please sign using this link: https://app.docusign.com/FF1234abcd-efgh-5678

Target to execute by Oct 1 to keep go-live timing. If procurement needs the 60-day clause as a non-negotiable, let us know immediately and I will escalate to Revenue Ops for accommodation.

Appreciate the collaboration — happy to hop on a 20-minute call if any item needs a walkthrough.
